statuses.title: SDPA sliding-window constraint silently dropped when attention_mask is None
statuses.note: The original fix (171da1c7, PR #877) is correct and I reproduced it end to end against clean out-of-process upstream references on transformers 5.15.1 / torch 2.13: with attn_implementation='sdpa', attention_mask=None, sliding_window=4, seq=12, patched logits are bit-identical to upstream for mistral (sum 7.7641603413794655 both), gemma3 (22.49240287952125 both, layer_types=['sliding_attention','sliding_attention']), cohere2 (1.5250016759855498 both) and phi3 (-6.6575579488126095 both), while the window-free control (sliding_window=64) gives visibly different values (5.1619938626, 18.4146024592, 1.7716508644, 0.2774928018). A seq sweep at the window boundary (seq=3,4,5,6,9 with sliding_window=4) is bit-exact, so the `target_length <= sliding_window` skip predicate at runtime/masking.py:370,381 has no off-by-one. HOWEVER the later compact-mask perf work (4e61b09d PR #925, d80d3f99 PR #954, Sep 6) reopened the same defect for the three families that now use vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask (mistral, ministral, gemma2): the builder elides the mask on the assumption that the family's patched SDPA forward applies the window, but the two preconditions are independently written predicates and diverge. Reproduced twice — gemma2 with attn_logit_softcapping=None (patched 19.25782148790313 == no-window reference 19.25782148790313, true reference 10.66509758651955) and mistral in train()+no_grad() with attention_dropout=0.1 and dropout=False (patched 4.206265495965454 == no-window reference 4.206265495965454, true reference 7.156000263028545). Filed as a finding.

statuses.title: Parity suite's upstream reference contaminated by unreverted module-global patches
statuses.note: parity_model_patches (_test_utils.py:256-303) now snapshots and restores the five rebindable module names plus the whole ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS object, and that restore works: I snapshotted every function, nn.Module class forward and attention registry across every loaded transformers.* module before and after `with parity_model_patches(model): pass` for llama, mistral, gemma2, gemma3, cohere2 and phi3 — zero attributes changed. tests/transformers/models/test_parity_harness.py (4 tests) passes. BUT the contamination the issue describes is still present in the suite as it actually runs: 21 sibling per-family test modules (test_cohere.py:33, test_gemma2.py:33, test_llama.py:33, test_mistral.py:36, ... ) call `apply_model_patches(model, eager_attention=True)` with no restore, and pytest collects them before test_parity.py alphabetically. Probed at test_parity setup after test_llama.py: modeling_llama.eager_attention_forward is opaque's vmap_eager_attention_forward, create_causal_mask is vmap_create_causal_mask, repeat_kv is vmap_repeat_kv. Demonstrated decisively by injecting a 5% scaling error into opaque's _grouped_eager_attention and re-running the whole models directory: only 5 of 26 families fail (phi3, qwen2, qwen3, qwen3_moe, smollm3 — exactly the families whose test file sorts after test_parity.py); the other 21 pass with a 5%-wrong attention because their 'upstream' reference runs the corrupted opaque shim. Filed as a finding.

statuses.title: Unregistered HF family silently skips the dropout/batchify contract
statuses.note: _router.py:131-149 now raises ConfigurationError for an unregistered family whenever the model is a transformers.PreTrainedModel and compat is on, logs at WARNING (not DEBUG) otherwise, and the DPTrainer docstring (_dp_trainer.py:829-834) was corrected; the error is not swallowed by DPTrainer (_dp_trainer.py:843-849 calls apply_model_patches unguarded). Verified with a bare FalconForCausalLM (falcon is unregistered): ConfigurationError 'opaque: compatibility/dropout/batchify patches require a registered transformers family; got falcon (FalconForCausalLM)'. Non-HF nn.Module still warns and proceeds, which is the intended escape hatch. Residual: peft.PeftModel is not a PreTrainedModel subclass, so a LoRA-wrapped unregistered HF family still fails open — verified: peft.get_peft_model(FalconForCausalLM(...)) through apply_model_patches raises nothing, logs only the warning, leaves nn.Dropout(p=0.3) and config.attention_dropout=0.3 intact, and never reaches the PeftModel batchify patch at _router.py:171-183 because the function returns at line 149. Filed as a finding.

statuses.title: test_sliding_window_parity never exercises a binding window
statuses.note: test_parity.py:304-339 now uses sliding_window=4 with seq_len=16 (_SLIDING_WINDOW=4, _SLIDING_WINDOW_SEQ_LEN=16 at :60-63), parametrizes use_attention_mask over [True, False] so the no-padding-mask SDPA path OPQ-337 described is exercised, and adds a vacuity guard (assert_logits_differ against a non-binding sliding_window=64 run, _test_utils.py:418-435) that would fire if the window were dropped entirely. Ran the models parity suite: 214 passed / 20 skipped. Two caveats that are NOT part of OPQ-341's claim but bound the value of this test: (a) _SLIDING_WINDOW_FAMILIES = {'ministral','mistral'} (test_parity.py:57) while cohere2, exaone4, gemma2, gpt_oss, mellum and olmo3 all ship a non-None config.sliding_window — gemma2 in particular is where the residual OPQ-337 defect I filed lives, and it has no binding-window parity case; (b) the test runs under the still-contaminated harness described in the #812 status, so its patched-vs-upstream half is weak for mistral/ministral (both test files sort before test_parity.py) — only the vacuity guard is unaffected. Filed the coverage gap as a low finding.

statuses.title: Gemma2 SDPA shim installed in the process-global attention registry
statuses.note: _family.py:67-97 (_scoped_attention_functions) clones the shared AttentionInterface into a module-private instance, copies its existing _local_mapping, tags it _opaque_scoped_to, and rebinds mod.ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS; _family.py:217-223 then writes 'sdpa' into that private instance. Verified in-process on transformers 5.15.1: before patching, modeling_llama.ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS is modeling_utils.ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS (True). After apply_gemma2_family_patches(), modeling_gemma2's registry is a fresh instance whose 'sdpa' is vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2, while modeling_llama's registry is still the shared object with the stock transformers.integrations.sdpa_attention.sdpa_attention_forward, and so is the shared module_utils instance and never-patched modeling_qwen2. After additionally patching llama, gemma2 keeps its own shim and the shared registry is still stock. The clone remains correct because AttentionInterface._global_mapping (flash/flex/paged/sdpa) is a class attribute that GeneralInterface.__getitem__ falls back to, and AttentionInterface.register() writes that class mapping, so later library-wide registrations stay visible to scoped modules. Modeling modules resolve the interface through the module global at call time (e.g. modeling_mistral.py:161 ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS.get_interface(...)), so the rebind takes effect. No residual.

statuses.title: Fused activation backward mutates saved gate/up activations in place
statuses.note: The fix takes the 'detect the second traversal' option from OPQ-343's own fix sketch rather than cloning: a ctx._opaque_backward_done latch at the top of Opaque_SwiGLU.backward (swiglu.py:250-253), Opaque_GeGLU_Exact.backward (geglu.py:248-251), Opaque_GeGLU_Approx.backward (geglu.py:514-519) and Opaque_LoRA_MLP.backward (lora.py:1119-1122), so a retained-graph re-traversal raises NotImplementedError instead of reading overwritten activations. I verified the mechanism itself on this torch 2.13 build with an equivalent pure-torch autograd.Function using setup_context: the first torch.autograd.grad(..., retain_graph=True) succeeds and the second raises NotImplementedError, confirming ctx attributes persist across traversals of the same node. The in-place overwrite itself is unchanged (lora.py:726-738, 860-861, 946-947 still hand storage-sharing gate/up views to act_backward_fused), so the guarantee now rests entirely on the latch. Caveats: (1) this host has no CUDA and the kernels are Triton-only (Opaque_SwiGLU.forward at swiglu.py:218-240 calls _fg_kernel unconditionally, no CPU fallback), so the numerical consequence and the new CUDA-marked tests could not be executed here; (2) the latch was added only to the four entry points OPQ-343 named — the wider sweep across the other fused kernels (rope_embedding, rms_norm, fused_add_rms_norm, moe, Opaque_LoRA_QKV, Opaque_LoRA_W) is tracked in open issue #898 and I did not re-report it.

findings.title: Compact SDPA sliding-window elision reopens OPQ-337: gemma2 with softcapping disabled attends to the full context
findings.claim: The perf work in 4e61b09d (PR #925) and d80d3f99 (PR #954) made mistral, ministral and gemma2 use vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask, which returns None (no mask at all) whenever _can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window (runtime/masking.py:78-107) holds, on the assumption that the family's patched SDPA forward applies the look-back limit itself. That assumption is encoded twice, in two independently written predicates, and they diverge. (a) vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2 (attention.py:670-738) consumes `sliding_window` only inside its `if softcap is not None:` branch (line 683); when Gemma2Attention passes softcap=self.attn_logit_softcapping=None (modeling_gemma2.py:282) it falls through to `return vmap_sdpa_attention_forward(...)` at line 729, whose signature has no sliding_window parameter at all — the window is dropped and plain causal SDPA runs. (b) The builder admits the elision when `not torch.is_grad_enabled() or config.attention_dropout == 0.0` (masking.py:103-105) while vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window requires the runtime `dropout == 0.0` (attention.py:297); in train mode under no_grad with a non-zero attention_dropout the builder elides and the forward declines. Nothing asserts that the forward actually applied what the builder skipped, so both paths fail open. This is exactly the defect OPQ-337 reported, in sibling paths that 171da1c7 (#877) fixed correctly and that later perf commits reopened.
findings.failure_scenario: Gemma2 with attn_logit_softcapping=None (a config people set precisely because softcapping is not expressible in fused SDPA/flash kernels), attn_implementation='sdpa' (the transformers default) and no attention_mask — the standard model(input_ids) shape in eval, perplexity and prefill code, and reachable from DPTrainer whenever the batch carries no attention_mask. Every sliding-attention layer attends to the entire causal prefix instead of the window, so the model trained or evaluated is not the architecture it claims to implement. Accounting is untouched.
evidence: End-to-end, transformers 5.15.1 / torch 2.13, tiny Gemma2 (hidden 64, 2 layers, default alternating layer_types=['sliding_attention','full_attention'], sliding_window=4, seq=12, attn_implementation='sdpa', attention_mask=None, attn_logit_softcapping=None), logits sum computed in separate processes on identical seeded weights: upstream reference 10.66509758651955, opaque-patched 19.25782148790313, upstream with the window disabled (sliding_window=64) 19.25782148790313 — the patched model reproduces the no-window reference to the last digit.
Same config with attn_logit_softcapping at its 50.0 default: reference 10.664953630010132 vs patched 10.664955383865163 (1.7e-6, fp32 noise) — the defect is confined to the softcap=None fallthrough.

Scoping: with an all-ones attention_mask the same softcap=None config matches exactly (12.104748404293787 both), and with attn_implementation='eager' it matches exactly (12.104748966979969 both) — the trigger profile is identical to OPQ-337's.

Unit level: vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2(module, q, k, v, None, scaling=1.0, softcap=None, sliding_window=3) on (1,2,8,4) tensors differs from a dense windowed reference by 1.1628184318542480 and from a dense NO-window reference by 1.1920928955078125e-07; the same call with softcap=1e9 matches the windowed reference to 1.19e-07.

Predicate-divergence path (b), tiny Mistral (sliding_window=4, seq=12, sdpa, attention_mask=None, attention_dropout=0.1, model.train() inside torch.no_grad(), apply_model_patches(..., dropout=False)): upstream 7.156000263028545, patched 4.206265495965454, upstream with sliding_window=64 4.206265495965454.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:683 `if softcap is not None:` and :729 `return vmap_sdpa_attention_forward(` — the fallthrough drops sliding_window; vmap_sdpa_attention_forward (attention.py:169-241) never reads it.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/runtime/masking.py:102-107 `and (not torch.is_grad_enabled() or getattr(config, "attention_dropout", None) == 0.0) and _query_length(input_embeds) > sliding_window` vs packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:297 `and dropout == 0.0`.

git show d80d3f99 -- .../models/gemma2.py adds `masking_module_patcher=apply_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_masking_patch` (models/gemma2.py:35); before that commit gemma2 used the generic builder, which materialized the window.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the elision and the application one predicate instead of two. Either (i) have vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask receive the family's attention-side precondition (pass the concrete forward, or a capability probe, and require exactly the same conditions: runtime dropout, softcap disposition, position_bias), or (ii) make the family SDPA forwards total for sliding windows — give vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2 a non-softcap branch that routes through _compact_sliding_window_sdpa when sliding_window is not None, and have vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window fall back to building the band mask itself (via _sdpa_sliding_window_mask) rather than to the window-blind vmap_sdpa_attention_forward. Add a debug assertion (or a fail-closed raise) when a compact-elided mask reaches a forward that will not apply the window. Extend test_parity.py::test_sliding_window_parity to gemma2 with attn_logit_softcapping parametrized over {50.0, None}, and add a component test for vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2 with softcap=None (the existing one, tests/transformers/components/test_attention.py:316-346, only covers softcap=1.0).

findings.title: Parity suite still compares patched against patched for 21 of 26 families — sibling test modules re-contaminate what #812 restores
findings.line: 33 (and test_cohere.py:33, test_cohere2.py:36, test_exaone4.py:36, test_gemma.py:33, test_gemma2.py:33, test_gemma3.py:43, test_glm4.py:33, test_gpt2.py:40, test_granite.py:36, test_mellum.py:74, test_ministral.py:36, test_mistral.py:36, test_olmo2.py:33, test_olmo3.py:33, test_attention_impls.py:38,95)
findings.claim: OPQ-338's fix hardened parity_model_patches so that the context it owns restores every module-level rebinding. It did not address the other producer of the same contamination: every per-family test module applies opaque's model patches at test scope with no restore, and pytest collects those files before test_parity.py in the same process (default alphabetical directory order). parity_model_patches therefore snapshots an already-patched module as its 'original' and restores it to that state, and build_patched_model_pair's 'unpatched' reference model runs opaque's own eager_attention_forward, repeat_kv and create_causal_mask/create_sliding_window_causal_mask. The parity evidence for every patches fix in this milestone is weaker than it looks, which is the exact consequence the issue predicted.
findings.failure_scenario: Any future numerical regression inside vmap_eager_attention_forward, vmap_repeat_kv, _grouped_eager_attention or the mask builders shifts the reference and the patched model identically and the suite stays green. Only the five families whose test file sorts after test_parity.py (phi3, qwen2, qwen3, qwen3_moe, smollm3) are actually compared against upstream.
evidence: Probe at test setup, `pytest test_llama.py test_parity.py -k llama`: for every test_parity llama case, transformers.models.llama.modeling_llama.eager_attention_forward -> opaque.api.patches.transformers.components.attention.vmap_eager_attention_forward, create_causal_mask -> opaque.api.patches.transformers.runtime.masking.vmap_create_causal_mask, repeat_kv -> opaque.api.patches.transformers.components.attention.vmap_repeat_kv.

Injected regression, 5% scaling error in opaque.api.patches.transformers.components.attention._grouped_eager_attention. `pytest test_parity.py -k eager-llama` ALONE: 1 failed ('llama [eager] forward parity failed'). `pytest test_llama.py test_parity.py -k "eager-llama or (llama and vmap)"`: 4 passed.

Same injection over the whole directory (`pytest packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models -p corrupt_plugin`): 5 failed, 209 passed — failures only test_forward_logits_parity[eager-{phi3,qwen2,qwen3,qwen3_moe,smollm3}], i.e. exactly the families whose per-family test file sorts after test_parity.py.
Collection order confirmed with --collect-only: test_attention_impls, test_cohere, ..., test_olmo3, THEN test_parity.py, test_parity_harness.py, then test_phi3, test_qwen*, test_smollm3.

test_parity_harness.py::test_reference_output_survives_a_patch_cycle cannot see this: it compares a reference built before the cycle with one built after, and both are equally contaminated; it also runs after test_parity.py.
packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/_test_utils.py:274-288 takes the snapshot at context entry, so an already-patched module is recorded as the original.
findings.fix_sketch: Reuse the isolation the fix already built: add a conftest.py under tests/transformers/models with an autouse fixture that snapshots and restores _FAMILY_MODULE_PATCH_NAMES + ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS + class forwards around every test (factor parity_model_patches' finally block into a reusable restore helper), or convert the per-family modules to use parity_model_patches / build_runtime_patched_model_pair inside a context. Then make the contamination detectable: add a harness test that asserts modeling_<family>.eager_attention_forward / create_causal_mask are the stock objects at the start of each parity test, and keep the injected-error check as a meta-test (mutate _grouped_eager_attention, assert the suite fails for every family).

findings.title: Gemma3 bidirectional attention: or_mask_function / and_mask_function are accepted and silently ignored by opaque's mask builders
findings.line: 159-315 (vmap_create_causal_mask: or_mask_function/and_mask_function parameters at :165-166 are never read) and 318-447 (vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask forwards them to a function that ignores them)
findings.claim: The same defect pattern as OPQ-337 — opaque's mask builder silently discards a constraint upstream applies — survives in a sibling path the #811 fix did not touch. vmap_create_causal_mask declares or_mask_function and and_mask_function in its signature and never uses them; vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask passes them down to that function (masking.py:389-390) and its own compact/generic SDPA short-circuit at masking.py:361-372 does not even check whether they are set before returning a plain band mask. transformers 5.15.1's Gemma3TextModel uses or_mask_function to implement bidirectional attention (modeling_gemma3.py:547-549) and blockwise/sliding overlays for packed inputs (modeling_gemma3.py:748-752), and gemma3 is a registered opaque family. block_sequence_ids is dropped the same way (it is absorbed by **kwargs).
findings.failure_scenario: Fine-tuning or evaluating a Gemma3 text model with use_bidirectional_attention=True (the EmbeddingGemma configuration) under DPTrainer: opaque's patched model silently runs plain causal (and causal-windowed) attention while upstream runs bidirectional, so the optimized objective is not the advertised architecture. No warning is emitted and no parity test sets the flag.
evidence: Reproduced on transformers 5.15.1 / torch 2.13 with a tiny Gemma3ForCausalLM (Gemma3TextConfig, hidden 64, 2 layers, layer_types=['sliding_attention','full_attention'], sliding_window=4, seq=12, eager, all-ones mask), logits sum on identical seeded weights: use_bidirectional_attention=True -> upstream 24.917816297362833, opaque-patched 13.034685771737713; use_bidirectional_attention=False -> 18.334294046406285 for both.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/runtime/masking.py:165-166 declares `or_mask_function=None, and_mask_function=None` and no line in the body of vmap_create_causal_mask (masking.py:186-315) references either name.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/runtime/masking.py:361-372: the SDPA short-circuit returns `_sdpa_sliding_window_mask(...)` / `None` without consulting or_mask_function, and_mask_function or block_sequence_ids (contrast _can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window at masking.py:99-101, which does check all three).

.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/transformers/models/gemma3/modeling_gemma3.py:547-549 sets mask_kwargs['or_mask_function'] and sliding_mask_kwargs['or_mask_function'] when config.use_bidirectional_attention, and :748-752 passes or_mask_function=blockwise_overlay(...) + and_mask_function=sliding_window_overlay(...).
findings.fix_sketch: Implement the two hooks in vmap_create_causal_mask the way transformers' masking_utils composes them (vectorized mask_function -> OR with or_mask_function -> AND with and_mask_function) using vmap-safe tensor ops, and make every short-circuit in vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask / vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask refuse to elide when either hook or block_sequence_ids is present. Until that lands, fail closed: raise ConfigurationError from the builders when a non-None or_mask_function/and_mask_function/block_sequence_ids arrives, so a bidirectional Gemma3 cannot silently train as a causal one. Add a gemma3 parity case with use_bidirectional_attention=True.

findings.title: Fail-closed guard for unregistered HF families does not see PEFT-wrapped models
findings.claim: The #814 fix decides whether to fail closed with `isinstance(model, transformers.PreTrainedModel)`. peft.PeftModel inherits torch.nn.Module + PushToHubMixin, not PreTrainedModel, so a LoRA-wrapped model of an unregistered HF family takes the warn-and-return branch at _router.py:144-149. detect_family still resolves the family correctly through PeftModel's attribute forwarding, so the router knows it is looking at an HF architecture it cannot patch and proceeds anyway. Two vmap-safety patches are lost, not one: disable_dropout (_router.py:165-168) and the PeftModel batchify patch (_router.py:171-183) are both below the early return. DP-LoRA on a Hugging Face causal LM is the primary documented Opaque workflow, so the escape hatch is wider than the one the fix intended for custom non-HF nn.Modules.
findings.failure_scenario: A user DP-fine-tunes a LoRA adapter on an unregistered HF family (e.g. falcon) through DPTrainer. No error, only a warning. Dropout survives, and under vmap(grad) with randomness='same' (_clipped_fun.py) every example in the batch shares one dropout mask, so per-example gradients differ from both ordinary training and the dropout-free configuration the trainer documents; the PeftModel batchify shim that makes the wrapper vmap-safe is also never applied. Privacy is unaffected — clipping still bounds sensitivity.
evidence: Reproduced on transformers 5.15.1 / peft 0.20.0: `supported_families()` does not contain 'falcon'. Bare FalconForCausalLM -> ConfigurationError 'opaque: compatibility/dropout/batchify patches require a registered transformers family; got 'falcon' (FalconForCausalLM)'. peft.get_peft_model(FalconForCausalLM(cfg), LoraConfig(...)) -> isinstance(pm, peft.PeftModel)=True, isinstance(pm, transformers.PreTrainedModel)=False, detect_family(pm)='falcon', apply_model_patches(pm) raises nothing and logs only WARNING 'opaque: no registered apply function for model family falcon; no model-level patches applied.'
After that call the model still has ('base_model.model.transformer.h.0.self_attention.attention_dropout', 0.3) and config.attention_dropout=0.3 / hidden_dropout=0.3.
packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/_router.py:149 `return` precedes both the dropout block (:165-168) and the PeftModel batchify block (:171-183).
packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/test_public_factory.py:548-563 only covers a bare PreTrainedModel subclass; no test wraps an unregistered family in PEFT.
findings.fix_sketch: Make _is_hf_pretrained_model unwrap PEFT: treat the model as an HF model when it is a PreTrainedModel, or when peft is importable and isinstance(model, peft.PeftModel) and the unwrapped base (get_base_model() / model.base_model.model) is a PreTrainedModel. Equivalently, key the decision off detect_family(model) returning a non-None model_type that is absent from the registry, which already works through the PEFT wrapper. Add a test that get_peft_model over an unregistered PreTrainedModel raises ConfigurationError.

findings.title: Binding sliding-window parity covers only mistral and ministral; the four other windowed families are untested
findings.claim: _SLIDING_WINDOW_FAMILIES = {'ministral', 'mistral'} but six registered families ship a non-None config.sliding_window on transformers 5.15.1 — cohere2 (4096), exaone4 (4096), gemma2 (4096), gpt_oss (128), mellum (1024) and olmo3 (4096) — plus gemma3, whose text config takes one when layer_types include sliding_attention. OPQ-337's own failure scenario named Gemma2, Gemma3 text, Cohere2 and Phi-3 explicitly. The one family whose SDPA forward has a sliding-window-specific shim with a fallthrough that drops the window (gemma2, see the first finding) is therefore the one with no binding-window parity case at all.
findings.failure_scenario: A sliding-window regression in any family other than mistral/ministral — including the live gemma2 softcap=None drop confirmed in this review — ships green. The suite's own 214-passing run on this tree is an example: it does not exercise a binding window for gemma2, cohere2, exaone4, olmo3, gpt_oss or gemma3.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:57 `_SLIDING_WINDOW_FAMILIES = {"ministral", "mistral"}`.

Enumerated default configs for all 26 supported_families() on transformers 5.15.1: cohere2 sliding_window=4096, deepseek_v4 128, exaone4 4096, gemma2 4096, gpt_oss 128, mellum 1024, ministral 4096, mistral 4096, olmo3 4096.

test_softcapping_parity (test_parity.py:342-...) pins attn_logit_softcapping=50.0 for gemma2/gemma3, so the softcap=None branch of vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2 has no end-to-end coverage either.
Ran the models parity suite on this tree: 214 passed, 20 skipped — with the gemma2 softcap=None window drop present.
findings.fix_sketch: Derive _SLIDING_WINDOW_FAMILIES from the family's config rather than a hand-maintained literal (include any family whose default config exposes a non-None sliding_window, or whose layer_types can contain 'sliding_attention'), keep the binding geometry and vacuity guard, and parametrize gemma2/gemma3 over attn_logit_softcapping in {50.0, None}.
